title: Iff-split of the IMO 2026 P5 answer: admissible f are x ↦ x + c
intent: Characterise the functions satisfying the IMO 2026 P5 inequality as exactly the affine family x ↦ x + c with c ≥ 0, by splitting Fact_condition f ↔ f ∈ answer into a forward direction closed from d_nonneg and g_const and a backward direction that is the verification lemma easy_dir.

parent.name: answer_correctness
parent.statement: theorem answer_correctness (f : ℝ → ℝ) (ha_pos : Assumption_pos f) : Fact_condition f ↔ f ∈ answer

children.name: d_nonneg
children.statement: lemma d_nonneg (f : ℝ → ℝ) (ha : Assumption_pos f) (hf : Fact_condition f) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 < y) : 0 ≤ f y - y
children.closed_by: by_contra; obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt (y / (-d)); have hpos := (orbit f ha hf hy n).1; linarith

children.name: g_const
children.statement: lemma g_const (f : ℝ → ℝ) (ha : Assumption_pos f) (hf : Fact_condition f) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : f x - x = f 1 - 1
children.closed_by: rcases eq_or_lt_of_le on the two d_nonneg facts; no_mixed eliminates the mixed cases; le_antisymm (pos_d_le f ha hf hx one_pos h10) (pos_d_le f ha hf one_pos hx hx0)

children.name: easy_dir
children.statement: lemma easy_dir (f : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hfc : ∀ x : ℝ, 0 < x → f x = x + c) : Fact_condition f
children.closed_by: rw [hfc x hx, hfc y hy]; constructor; per conjunct a calc chain closed by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x - y - c)] and positivity

applicability.goal_shape: a biconditional P f ↔ f ∈ answer where answer is the closed family {f | ∃ c, side c ∧ ∀ x, 0 < x → f x = g x c}; the forward direction exhibits the parameter c from a single evaluation and the backward direction is a verification lemma
applicability.use_when: the family is in closed form and every member verifies P independently of the uniqueness argument, and the parameter is determined by one evaluation (here f 1 - 1) plus a constancy lemma
applicability.avoid_when: the two directions share a deep argument (the split duplicates it); the family is not given in closed form (no single witness to exhibit); the parameter is not determined by one evaluation (needs an extra uniqueness lemma)

consequences: The split creates exactly two goals, one per direction of the iff. The forward direction additionally creates a witness obligation (refine ⟨f 1 - 1, ?_, ?_⟩): prove 0 ≤ f 1 - 1 (discharged by d_nonneg) and f x = x + (f 1 - 1) (discharged by g_const). If g_const were missing or too weak the forward direction would not close; if answer were not a plain ∃ family the backward rintro ⟨c, hc, hfc⟩ would not be a one-liner. The two directions are otherwise independent.
